newsitem.title: UK: Hanson sees building units set for upturn.
newsitem.headline: Hanson sees building units set for upturn.

text.p: British-based building materials and services group Hanson Plc said on Tuesday that signals of a partial recovery in British markets were continuing to emerge and that trading prospects in the U.S. remained firm.

In comments on its current trading, less than a month before the final demerger that will complete the former conglomerate's four-way split, the group said an upturn in British housing starts in the last quarter of 1996 had boosted its national brick deliveries by 12 percent year-on-year in the period.
However, trading conditions remained pressured in its British electrical products and aggregates units, Hanson added.
"Total UK demand for aggregates in 1996 was around the same level as 10 years ago at about 215 million tonnes. The aggregates market is believed to be at the bottom of its cycle," Hanson said.
"The increase in housing starts offers the prospect of future improvement in Hanson Electrical's UK markets, but domestic wiring accessories contine to face pressure from imports," it added.
While electrical's overseas sales, which made up about a third of its 1995/96 sales, remained buoyant, Hanson called the picture for brick markets in continental Europe "subdued".
In its large crane hire business, Grove Crane, Hanson said that although markets remained favourable in demand terms, "the company is facing aggressive pricing tactics from some of its competitors".

In the United States, where the group's main interest is in the Cornerstone heavy materials business, Hanson said it hoped to benefit from a continued steady performance and anticipated no downturn in the U.S. economy big enough to have a significant impact on its operations.
"Cornerstone's strong position in states with growing economies, together with the benefit of recent capital expenditure, should have a favourable impact," Hanson added.
